attractions.name: Takht-i-Bahi
attractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring the remarkably well-preserved remains of an ancient Buddhist monastery complex from the Gandhara era.

attractions.name: Jamal Garhi
attractions.description: Another significant Buddhist archaeological site from the Gandhara civilization, with monastery ruins and stupas.

attractions.name: Mardan Museum
attractions.description: A museum housing Gandhara-era artifacts and sculptures excavated from the surrounding archaeological sites.

food_places.name: Mardan Chapli Kebab houses
food_places.specialty: Mardan is famous nationwide for its chapli kebab

food_places.name: Local tea houses and bakeries
food_places.specialty: Traditional Pashtun tea and baked snacks

transportation.notes: Round-trip taxi fare typical for the archaeological site visit

weather_info.climate_type: Semi-arid, continental climate with hot summers and cool winters

travel_tips.tip: Mardan is a convenient stopover between Peshawar and the Swat valley, worth combining into one trip.
Hire a local taxi for a half-day to visit both Takht-i-Bahi and Jamal Garhi together, since they're relatively close to each other.
Standard travel precautions apply; stick to well-known archaeological sites and city areas.
Visit Takht-i-Bahi in the morning for cooler temperatures and better light over the hillside ruins.

history.founded: The surrounding region has ancient roots in the Gandhara civilization, over 2,000 years old
history.city_history: Mardan sits at the heart of the ancient Gandhara region, once a major center of Buddhist learning and art, evidenced by the remarkably preserved monastery ruins at Takht-i-Bahi. The modern city developed as an important agricultural and trading center in the Peshawar valley.
history.province_history: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has historically been a crossroads between South and Central Asia, home to the ancient Gandhara civilization, and later part of the Mughal Empire, Sikh Empire, and British India, before joining Pakistan in 1947. It was renamed from the North-West Frontier Province to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2010.
